# SB-1019 - Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Hazard description
- Background: Recent checks of the dust collection system serving the Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) identified an elevated dust collector pressure drop alarm setpoint being reached during normal operation. The dust load on the collector can increase quench oil mist settling in downstream fabric filters and ductwork. Accumulated oil-dust deposits in the collector or downstream plenums present a combustible mixture that can be ignited by hot particulates, electrostatic discharge, or frictional heating from clogged blowers, creating a quench oil fire risk in the heat treat area.
- Observation: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. This alarm level has been confirmed by maintenance logs and transient capture during last shutdowns, indicating the collector has reached a resistance to airflow consistent with significant media loading. A sustained condition at this alarm indicates a decreased capture efficiency for oil mist and increased potential for deposit accumulation. Operators must assume the presence of oil-impregnated dust layers in the system when this alarm value is recorded.
- Step rationale: The alarm value of 1510 Pa is used as the operational trigger to prevent extended operation under high loading conditions. Allowing continued operation beyond this level increases the risk window for ignition events and reduces the ability of emergency mitigation measures to control a fire. Actions below are intended to eliminate fuel sources, interrupt ignition paths, and restore filtration performance.

Affected equipment
- Primary: Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) and its dedicated dust collector and ductwork.
- Adjacent systems: Local ventilation and plenum serving the heat treat bay, portable air handling equipment used for maintenance, and any temporary quench oil application devices that share recovery or drainage systems with EQ-P3-L4-SB03.
- Refer to documented maintenance and machine history in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for past filter change records and SB-1038 for related quench oil incident analyses. Operational steps and permitted startup sequence adjustments are detailed in SOP-P3-L4-02.

Required controls
- Immediate actions upon alarm:
  - Stop production feeds to the shot blast cabinet and place EQ-P3-L4-SB03 in safe shutdown per SOP-P3-L4-02.
  - Isolate sources of quench oil flow to the cabinet and associated conveyors. Verify isolation with visual confirmation and log the action in the equipment downtime record.
  - Notify maintenance and safety supervision and tag the dust collector out of service pending inspection and cleaning. Record the alarm occurrence and actions taken in the shift log and in the equipment corrective action record (see MM-P3-L4-SB03).
- Inspection and cleaning:
  - Qualified maintenance shall perform a visual and hands-off inspection of the collector internals, downstream plenums, duct transitions, and blower housings. Look specifically for oil-wetted dust deposits, smoldering marks, or particulate bridging at seams and transitions. Document findings and attach photographs to the maintenance report.
  - Remove and properly dispose of oil-contaminated filters and accumulated deposits per the hazardous waste handling procedures referenced in MM-P3-L4-SB03. Do not attempt compressed-air cleaning of oil-impregnated media.
- Restart conditions:
  - Return-to-service is permitted only after cleaning and remediation are completed, blower vibration and temperature are verified to be within normal limits per OEM guidance, and the collector demonstrates a cleared pressure drop below the alarm threshold during a controlled test run outlined in SOP-P3-L4-02. Record the test run results in the equipment test log.
- Engineering and administrative controls:
  - Implement routine inspection checkpoints for visible oil carryover at the cabinet exhaust, with findings entered into the preventive maintenance log in MM-P3-L4-SB03.
  - Update SOP-P3-L4-02 to include the 1510 Pa alarm response steps and recordkeeping requirements. Ensure operators and maintenance personnel review the updated SOP before returning EQ-P3-L4-SB03 to production.
  - Prohibit hot work, open flames, or ignition source introduction in the affected bay until a safety clearance is issued by safety supervision and recorded.

Examples and scenarios
- Example scenario A: During an end-of-shift changeover, the operator observes the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. The operator initiates shutdown per SOP-P3-L4-02, isolates oil feeds, and logs the event. Maintenance finds oil-wetted filter media and schedules replacement. Production resumes only after documentation of cleaning and a successful controlled test run.
- Example scenario B: If the alarm is intermittent, log each occurrence and increase inspection frequency until a pattern is established. Treat every occurrence as a potential hazard and follow immediate actions above until trend analysis from MM-P3-L4-SB03 indicates otherwise.

Records to keep
- Shift log entries documenting alarm occurrence, actions taken, and personnel notified.
- Maintenance inspection report with photos and measurements attached to MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Filter replacement and disposal records linked to the hazardous waste manifest or internal disposal log.
- Return-to-service test run results and signoff per SOP-P3-L4-02.
- Incident follow-up and root cause analysis documentation if any ignition, smoldering, or fire was observed, with cross-reference to SB-1038 for similar event learnings.

Effective date
- Effective: Upon issuance. All operations, maintenance, and safety personnel assigned to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 must comply with the required controls and update their local procedure checklists to reflect this bulletin.
